title: The Hero Squad of Justice
text: “Can you really call that fight ‘teamwork’? It feels more like they’re practicing assassination techniques… I don’t know about me, but it just doesn’t seem like what a hero’s battle should be…”
When Big Sister turns to Ren’s companions, they shake their heads.

“Before Black Thunder joined, we were taught to dodge monster attacks as much as possible… but now, it’s basically just Ren-sama and Black Thunder running the show, so to speak… We just practice dodging and honing our conversational skills to verbally exploit our opponents’ weaknesses.”
“Even against monsters you can’t communicate with?”
“Yes…”
That sounds pretty tough.
“Sadeena-nee was just messing around, wasn’t she?”
“Wouldn’t it be fun if you tried it for real, Raphtalia-chan?”
“No way.”
“It’s your bad luck that you showed up right in front of Firo… You’re all going to be Firo’s dinner!”
And with that, Filo-tan strikes a pose just like Ren and Black Thunder.
“Filo, that’s not right. For one thing, you’re not verbally exploiting their weaknesses—that’s a death threat.”
“…Filo was just mimicking what he said. The Sword Hero looked incredibly bored.”
“Well, those types can’t stand posers, after all.”
“Posers?”

My Father sighs at my exhausted-looking Big Sister. By the way, “poser” is a slang term used to describe someone who claims to be a fan but doesn’t really understand the genre and has only a superficial grasp of it. I, too, sometimes feel that way about people who blab on and on about Filolial-sama even though they don’t really understand her. Mainly the Griffin, Dragon, and Takt folks.
“Hmm?”

“It’s the same in that they’re declaring they’ll defeat her, but the tone is different. Well, Raphtalia did her best… I’ll have a talk with Ren’s companions later, so please head back to the companion exchange.”
“Lord Naofumi…”
“Sadeena, don’t get too carried away—make sure you don’t become a burden to Raphtalia.”
“Oh my, I wonder if the messenger from Kairai was no good after all?”

Big Sister’s older sister seems to be enjoying herself. Well, she doesn’t seem to be up to anything suspicious, though. The thing Ren and Itsuki need to be careful about is making sure they don’t break the seal on the Spirit Tortoise and the others.

I have a feeling that Black Thunder will definitely react to the phrase “must not break the seal” and will refrain from doing so. According to Father, it’s not in Ren’s or Black Thunder’s character to break seals unnecessarily.

Anyway, we’ve settled on leaving Ren’s party members in the capable hands of Father, who can reason with them. We mustn’t trouble my Father too much, right? Oh? It feels like various people in my head—my Father, my sister, and others—are saying, “You’re the last person who should be saying that,” but I won’t cause any trouble like that.
“Ah, Motoyasu-sama!”
Just then, Yuki-chan arrived with Itsuki in tow.
“Kwaa!”
Kou spotted his Big Sister and ran over to her, looking delighted.
“So it’s you, Kou-san. I see you’ve just come back from hunting with the Bow Hero.”
“Kwaa!”
Kou rubbed his cheek against his Big Sister’s face. As expected, Kou really takes to her.
“Yuki-chan, how are things going?”
“No problems at all. I just ran around patrolling the island as per Itsuki-san’s instructions. It’s boring because Kou’s so slow.”
Yuki-chan is looking over at Filo-tan. Come to think of it, didn’t they have some kind of race?

At that moment… I suddenly remembered the time when Yuki-chan and Itsuki clashed after they swapped party members. Itsuki had tried to “sidestep”—that is, steal a monster another adventurer was trying to defeat—but Yuki-chan had intercepted him.
I turn my gaze toward Itsuki. It looks like Itsuki is having a cheerful conversation with Fleon-chan and Leiska.
“Wasn’t Itsuki attacking monsters that other adventurers were trying to defeat, just to get EXP?”
“No, he wasn’t. On the contrary, he kept observing them intently and was offering advice to adventurers who seemed to be struggling because the monsters were too strong.”
Oh? Itsuki has really grown a lot since meeting Fleon-chan.
“He said, ‘There’s no evil on this island… it’s such a peaceful place.’”
Mm-hmm. It’s a good sign that neither Ren nor Itsuki seem likely to cause any major trouble.
“Did you fight the island’s lord?”
“Yes, we did. Following Itsuki’s instructions, Yuki weakened the lord, and then I delivered the finishing blow.”
“The finishing move, you say?”
“Yes. Apparently, it’s proper etiquette to unleash a finishing move on a boss. Yuki doesn’t quite understand that, does she?”

Yuki-chan is tilting her head in confusion. It’s a finishing move, isn’t it? It’s not that I don’t understand it either. I used to put on quite a show with those moves in the Zeltoble Arena. It really grabs the audience’s attention.
“To put it in terms Yuki-chan can understand, it’s like the dramatic build-up during a close race.”

“I-I see! I, Yuki, have finally grasped the etiquette of Mr. Itsuki! But isn’t there a difference between that and simply pulling away after a quick lead, or winning by a feather’s breadth? Motoyasu-sama, which is it?”

“If the goal is to show your opponent a difference in ability so great they might as well give up, then it’s a blowout. It would be rude to make it look like a nail-biter when you’re actually winning comfortably.”

“True, holding back would be rude. There’s no need for unnecessary consideration… Since the opponent is so far outclassed, it’s a subtle way of telling them to give up! It’s actually quite refreshing.”
As expected, when I explain things to Yuki-chan using racing terms, she catches on very quickly.

“That’s one way to interpret it, but for the one being attacked, wouldn’t that be overkill after they’ve already been beaten to a pulp? It’s no fun at all. Couldn’t you say he’s just getting drunk on the thrill of delivering the finishing blow?”

My Father, who had been listening to Yuki-chan and me from a distance, chimed in. Indeed, knowing Itsuki, that’s entirely possible. But let’s ask Yuki-chan about an important aspect of Itsuki’s growth.
“So, did Itsuki try to show Yuki-chan just how strong he is?”
“Not at all.”
Hmm… It seems Itsuki is growing up properly after all. I suppose having Fleon-chan around is really helping him become a better person. That’s a good sign.
“Sigh… It seems Ryo and Itsuki are similar in some ways, even if they’re heading in different directions. I have a feeling tomorrow’s going to be exhausting too, but I guess I’ll call it a day here…”
And so, I finished swapping partners with Itsuki, while my Father and the others finished swapping partners with Ren.
This happened a few hours later. I was playing tag with Yuki-chan on the beach when…
“These Filolial Masks can see right through you lot—selling shoddy jewelry as high-end items and charging a fortune for them!”
“Please admit your guilt honestly.”
“F-fueeeee…”

Huh? It sounds like I can hear a voice that sounds just like Fleon-chan coming from the direction of the market? Drawn by the sound, I headed toward the market and looked over. There, Fleon-chan and her friends—all wearing masks—were striking dramatic poses on the roof of a building, pointing directly at the merchants in the market.
“Even if the entire nation fails to see through it… the heroic team of justice, the Filolial Masks, will never let it slide!”
With that, Fleon-chan strikes a pose, and Itsuki follows suit by drawing his bow.
“Well… as long as our eyes are upon this island, for the sake of its people, we cannot tolerate the likes of you. Start selling at a fair price immediately.”
“I wish you’d cut the nonsense! We’re just trying to run a business here… Considering the shipping costs, it’s only natural that the price goes up accordingly, isn’t it?”
The merchant being confronted is acting as if he couldn’t care less. To top it off, he raises one hand, and burly men emerge from the back of the store.
“You’re interfering with our business! If you don’t cut it out, you’re going to get hurt… aren’t you?”
Oh, what a reckless and unscrupulous merchant.
“Well, I never… To resort to such violent behavior just because I presented the facts—I’m so dumbfounded I’m at a loss for words.”
“As for evidence… a look at your shop is more than enough… You understand that, don’t you, Ms. Leiska?”
“Waaah… y-yes. No matter what, passing off shoddy goods as high-end products is definitely not okay…”
“You still don’t get it even after all that…? Well, I suppose there’s no helping it. You lot! Do it!”
“‘Ooooh!’”
And with that, the burly men standing behind the merchant rush toward Fleon-chan and the others. However, those men were immediately rendered unable to fight.
“Stun Shot…”

When Itsuki fired an arrow at the burly men, they were unable to dodge and were hit between the eyes. While they weren’t all dead, they seemed to have been rendered immobile. They fell one after another with a thud.
“Whoa…”
“That’s awesome…”
“That shop over there was a real rip-off, wasn’t it?”
“Huh? Does that shop sell shoddy goods?　No wonder it broke so quickly… I knew it.”
The adventurers among the onlookers nodded in agreement, as if they’d suspected as much.
“D-Doing something like this—do you even know what’s lurking behind us, you lot?!”
The cornered merchant glared at Fleon and the others with hatred, shouting as he tried to flee, but Fleon leaped up and grabbed him right then and there.
“L-Let me go! You… Ugh!”
“Evil must be punished. We’ll just hand him over to the guards, but it’s best for us not to linger here…”
Fleon-chan, wearing a mask, kept the merchant pinned down while scanning the area.
“Ah! There’s the Shield Hero! Yes, you over there!”

Pointing in that direction, I saw my Father—who had been watching the commotion from the sidelines with a look of exasperation—standing there with my Big Sisters. The crowd parted swiftly around my Father, forming a circle.
“Tsk!”
My Father was about to turn his back on Fleon-chan and run off when our eyes met. Our gazes locked right there.

Ah, so this means he’s leaving the rest to me! “Leave it to me!” I said with a beaming smile and a thumbs-up, and my Father did a 180-degree spin, then walked back toward Fleon-chan and the others with an exasperated look on his face. Hmm? Was I wrong?
“How should I put this… Sigh…”
“Don’t say it! Seriously, these guys are such a pain…”
“Oh my—what a hassle.”
“Sadeena, if you think so, you figure it out.”
“Well, Naofumi-chan got picked for the job, so what can you do?”
“Damn it. Next time, I’m going to make sure you’re the one who cleans up the mess.”
“Oh my—”
“…If I keep repeating that line, he probably won’t treat me like a combatant and leave it to me…”
Muttering under his breath, my Father took custody of the merchant from Fleon-chan.
“The peace of this island… is being watched over by the Filolial Masks! Well then!”
With that, Fleon-chan took off high into the sky with Itsuki and Leiska on her back.
“Whoa…”
A sparse round of applause broke out. Amidst it all, Father looked at the merchant with pity in his eyes.
“He even hired a bodyguard to run his shady business… Yeah, this is definitely a scam. Totally under the table.”
Saying that, Father examined the items the merchant had been selling and nodded in agreement.
“N-no! We’re the victims here!”
“Hmm… By the way—”

As Father spoke, the merchant turned even paler than when he’d been confronted by Fleon and the others, and he bowed his head, begging for mercy. It seemed Father made some kind of proposal, and the merchant closed his shop with a smile. I’m sure he’ll start doing good business from now on.
“That settles the matter, then!”
Fleon-chan, who had taken off her mask without anyone noticing, stood near my Father and the others, her chest puffed out with pride. Of course, Itsuki and Leiska—in her pig form—were nearby as well.
“You lot…”
My Father furrowed his brow and glared at Fleon-chan and the others.
“What right do these people have to say such things…”
“Getting dragged into a masked hero’s mess is this much of a hassle…? But it’s far better than running away now and leaving this to Motoyasu.”
“It would only make the situation worse, after all.”
Of course! If they went on a rampage, it’d be total destruction, right? We’ve seen that happen before.
“So… Ren and Black Thunder… why are they standing by the hotel wall with their arms crossed, staring at us…? Do they think they look cool doing that?”
Father has sharp eyes, doesn’t he? It seems he knows exactly where Ren is.
“Father—what’s wrong?”
“Filo… were you eating at the food stall and didn’t see all this commotion…?”
“Hmm?”
That’s what happened that day. Starting the next day… it was quite memorable when the good-luck charms for the island’s success—the ones I’d seen in the first world—went on sale.
